title: UK rank-and-rent and local lead-generation research
decision: Determine whether UK rank-and-rent is investable in 2026, which city-niche combinations are most credible, and which operating and revenue model survives current search, platform and regulatory constraints.

googleAdsScope.method: One explicit service plus city phrase for every niche-city pair under the United Kingdom target, plus each generic service phrase and its near-me form under the same target. Nine city geo targets were then screened with 16 generic priority services, followed by expanded explicit and local-geo variants. A final depth pass broadened four priority market cells and separately measured buyer-acquisition and platform-brand queries. These screens overlap and are never added into demand.

methods: Google Ads Keyword Planning historical metrics
Local-geo and priority-query cross-checks with retained monthly series
Read-only Companies House profile, filing-history and filed-account capture for five lead marketplaces and selected suppliers in four local opportunity groups
Read-only Companies House filing capture and manual PDF transcription for Yell, FMB, Airtasker UK, Houzz UK and selected identity checks, retaining raw artifacts outside the public site
Purposive 40-product landscape across search, directories, marketplaces, owned-media groups, direct lead supply, agencies, trust schemes, fulfilment and operating infrastructure
Consumer-journey and participant-role expansion using current government guidance, UK attitudes research and opened operator workflow evidence
Buyer-acquisition Google Ads screen separated from consumer service demand and interpreted as advertiser-attention evidence rather than buyer counts
Live-web verification of official Google policies, UK regulator guidance, local-search research, marketplace models, service-price anchors and current result competitors
Public operator case studies and interviews retained with their self-reporting and commercial-incentive limitations
Mechanism-level AI-disruption analysis covering answer substitution, generated-content supply, agent qualification, operating leverage, verified data, physical fulfilment, and platform dependence
AI scores use a zero-to-five exposure or advantage scale by dimension and are not summed into one recommendation
A directional live web-result sample for selected city-niche pairs; this is not a personalised or geolocated Google local-pack audit
Volume-weighted CPC calculated as sum of searches multiplied by CPC divided by total searches
Paid-search-value proxy calculated as search volume multiplied by average CPC; it is a comparison device, not obtainable revenue
exclusions: Automated or geolocated Google result scraping
Unverified claims of profit, conversion, tenant demand or rankability
limitations: Average monthly searches are rounded trailing historical averages, not traffic forecasts.

Explicit city-query results describe phrases typed under a UK target; local-geo results describe generic phrases measured inside selected city geo targets. The disagreement between them is evidence to investigate rather than a reason to combine them.
Generic, near-me and explicit-city datasets overlap and must not be added together.
Google Ads can group close variants and can return zero where demand is sparse or withheld. Zero is not evidence of no demand.
Paid competition, CPC and top-of-page bids describe an advertising auction, not organic SEO difficulty, lead price, job revenue or profit.

Companies House data are company-filed registry evidence. Disclosure varies, the registrar does not comprehensively verify filed facts, and neither a filing nor a discovery match proves current trading quality, service coverage or willingness to buy leads.
The Companies House organisation set is deliberately selected rather than statistically sampled. Related entities and trading-identity mismatches remain explicitly flagged.

The platform financial comparison combines entities with different year ends, geographic scope, product mix and disclosure. Its revenue total is evidence of scale, not a market-size estimate or league table.
Buyer-intent and platform-brand query baskets overlap. Brand searches include consumers and navigation and must not be interpreted as supplier-signup demand.

The operator atlas is a purposive strategic sample of products rather than independent legal entities; related brands are identified in the text and first-party price, scale and outcome claims retain their marketing-source limitation.
The participant map describes recurring roles and proof requirements; it is not an employment census and no provider is assumed to perform every role in-house.
Market-dossier lead-price bands, buyer segments and capital scenarios are explicitly modelled hypotheses pending interviews and cohort evidence.
The 35-phrase city basket is a consistent comparison basket, not the complete local-services economy of each city.
The public UK rank-and-rent evidence base is dominated by self-reported operator marketing and anecdotes; no audited representative UK benchmark was found.
Current search-result discovery is directional and non-personalised; local packs, ads, device, location and history can change the actual result set.
Legal and regulator guidance is operational research, not legal advice.
Platform and model capabilities do not establish economic adoption, UK lead conversion, buyer acceptance, or captured operator margin.
No first-party generative-search conversion, AI-assisted lead-quality, generated-page maintenance, or buyer renewal cohort was available.
